question.text: Why are stock market indices significant as underlying assets for derivatives?

answer.text: They allow investors to take a view on or hedge against the overall market movement without trading individual stocks
They guarantee profits for derivative traders since indices always rise over time
They eliminate the need for individual stock analysis
They are easier to manipulate than individual stock prices

explanation.text: The Logic: Index derivatives are useful for hedging market (systematic) risk and for taking bullish or bearish views on the overall market through stock or index futures, without having to trade individual stocks. The Trap: Indices do not always rise — they can fall. Index derivatives do not guarantee profits, and they do not remove the need for individual stock analysis when an investor wants stock-specific exposure. Note: The workbook frames index derivatives around two source-backed use-cases — hedging portfolio risk and taking long/short directional views — rather than around liquidity or manipulation claims.
